title: HTML & CSS · The Box Model Decoded

scenes.line1: Why do layouts break so often?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why your layout suddenly breaks? What’s really causing those weird spacing issues?

scenes.label: Box
scenes.sub: Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin.
scenes.say: The answer is the box model. Every element on a page is a box made of content, padding, border, and margin.
Let’s break it down. First, you have the content. Next comes padding, then the border, and finally the margin outside.

left.title: Default
items: Padding and border add extra size

scenes.say: By default, width only covers the content. But with border-box, width includes padding and border. This makes responsive design way easier.

scenes.question: Does margin affect element width?
scenes.wrong: Yes, margin is part of width.
scenes.right: No, margin adds space outside the box, not to its width.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic interview trap: Does margin affect the width of an element? Nope. Margin adds space outside the box, not to its actual width.
